profile.name: gpuStack
profile.description: GPU stack shape for GKE GPU node pools — how the driver is installed and which device plugin advertises nvidia.com/gpu. The GPU Operator itself installs no driver on COS in either value. "gke-default" (the default) is the default-provisioned cluster: GKE's bundled driver install plus GKE's managed device plugin as the advertiser (opt-out label absent everywhere), with the operator's plugin disabled. "bundle-installer" is the opt-out pool shape (gke-no-default-nvidia-gpu-device-plugin=true, pools created with gpu-driver-version=disabled): the GPU Operator's device plugin is the sole advertiser, and the bundle-carried gcp-driver-installer component (issue #1716) supplies the driver — the version is pinned in the recipe and upgrades roll with the bundle. A hand-applied standalone nvidia-driver-installer DaemonSet is not a named mode: it is the same pool shape with an unmanaged installer — delete it and select bundle-installer (the bundle's DaemonSet shares its name and Helm will not adopt the pre-existing object). bundle-installer additionally verifies the pool's actual gpuDriverInstallationConfig against the K8s.gke-gpu-pools.gpu-driver-installation snapshot reading (supplied via --gke-gpu-pools), so a pool carrying the opt-out label without also having been created with gpu-driver-version=disabled fails closed instead of resolving as bundle-installer.

profile.name: gpuStack
profile.description: Who owns the GPU stack on OKE node pools. "oci-managed" (the default) is the Oracle-managed cluster: the GPU node image supplies the driver and toolkit, and OKE's NvidiaGpuPlugin add-on advertises nvidia.com/gpu — the GPU Operator installs none of the three. "operator-managed" is a bring-your-own driverless image with the add-on removed: the GPU Operator installs driver, toolkit, and device plugin, and the DRA driver reads the operator install path. MOFED is host-supplied in both values (Oracle and BYO images alike) — network-operator never deploys ofedDriver on OKE. The hybrid image-driver + operator-plugin shape is deliberately not declared (no consumer; the two-value model lets one control-plane signal qualify both axes).

A hand-applied standalone nvidia-driver-installer DaemonSet is not a named mode: it is the same pool shape with an unmanaged installer — delete it and select bundle-installer (the bundle's DaemonSet shares its name and Helm will not adopt the pre-existing object). bundle-installer additionally verifies the pool's actual gpuDriverInstallationConfig against the K8s.gke-gpu-pools.gpu-driver-installation snapshot reading (supplied via --gke-gpu-pools), so a pool carrying the opt-out label without also having been created with gpu-driver-version=disabled fails closed instead of resolving as bundle-installer.

profile.name: gpuStack
profile.description: Who owns the GPU stack on OKE node pools. "oci-managed" (the default) is the Oracle-managed cluster: the GPU node image supplies the driver and toolkit, and OKE's NvidiaGpuPlugin add-on advertises nvidia.com/gpu — the GPU Operator installs none of the three. "operator-managed" is a bring-your-own driverless image with the add-on removed: the GPU Operator installs driver, toolkit, and device plugin, and the DRA driver reads the operator install path. MOFED is host-supplied in both values (Oracle and BYO images alike) — network-operator never deploys ofedDriver on OKE. The hybrid image-driver + operator-plugin shape is deliberately not declared (no consumer; the two-value model lets one control-plane signal qualify both axes).
